title: FarikTeam
description: A team and everything the human configures about it, stored as .farik/team.yaml and read by the governor on every decision. See docs/SPEC.md sections 3, 5.12, 5.14 and 5.16, and decision D18 in docs/plans/project-plan.md.

name.description: What the human calls this team.

agents.description: Two agents at least, and at most seven that are not retired: a retired agent stays so that its past events still name someone, and does not count. The seven, and three more rules, are validate_team's rather than this schema's, because a schema cannot count only some items and typify cannot generate a usable type from an array that carries a `contains`: ids are unique, and the team has an active Product Manager and an active Software Developer.

prepare.description: Installs and builds, in the sandbox image with the task's worktree mounted and the network on, for at most 15 minutes; reused while the task branch's committed tree and this text are unchanged. Left out, skipped.

start.description: Starts the app, in a preview container of the sandbox image with the task's worktree mounted and the network off.

port.description: The port the app serves on inside its container.

path.description: The page to open first. Left out, /.

preview.description: How Farik opens the project's app for the ui_ux_designer (ADR 0026, the founder's D2): set once in Settings, under How to open your app. Without it a Designer's task is not assigned and a design review waits. Templates leave it out.

mcpServer.description: One connector an agent's task sessions get (spec 5.6). A builtin one is its name alone. A custom one says how it is started (stdio: command and args) or reached (http: url and headers), the names of the agent's keys it is given, and the label of each of its tools. validate_team checks what this schema does not, each at its own field: transport is required with source custom and absent with builtin; command and args go with stdio only; url and headers with http only; command with stdio and url with http are required; a command holding a / starts with one (command_not_absolute); a url holds no userinfo or query (url_holds_secret); a header names only a key in credential_keys (header_key_unknown); a custom name is not farik or a builtin's (connector_name_reserved); and one name appears once on an agent (connector_name_twice).

name.description: The connector's name on this agent, and its tools' mcp__<name>__ prefix: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, never an underscore. validate_team refuses a builtin one Farik does not ship with unknown_connector; the one it ships is playwright.

source.description: Where the connector's definition comes from: builtin, shipped in the farik binary; custom, added by the user to this agent.

transport.description: How a custom connector is reached: stdio, a program Farik starts on the host; http, a web address spoken to over streamable HTTP. The old SSE transport is not supported.

command.description: The program a stdio connector is started with: a name found on PATH, or a full path. validate_team refuses a relative path such as ./server or bin/mcp (command_not_absolute), which would be looked for in the folder the connector runs in.

args.description: The stdio connector's arguments. Never a secret: keys reach the program as environment variables.

url.description: The http connector's address. It is written here as it is, so it holds no userinfo and no query.

headers.description: Headers sent to an http connector, each a template that may hold {KEY} for a key in credential_keys and nothing else, filled in at launch.

credential_keys.description: The names of this agent's keys the connector is given. Their values are kept in the keychain or a private file, never here.

tools.description: Every tool the connector listed when it was connected, with the user's label. A tool it lists later is refused until it is connected again.

connectorTag.description: A connector tool's label (spec 5.6): network, it only reads; external_effect, it changes something outside the sandbox and asks the human; denied, never offered.

role.description: The role an agent is instantiated from. `human` is a role a contract may name as a reviewer, never a role an agent holds.

id.description: A kebab-case slug of the display name, unique within the team. Events and contracts refer to an agent by it, so it never changes.

persona.description: A few lines of character added to the role's system prompt. It never grants anything.

avatar.description: The name of a shipped avatar or a path under .farik/team/avatars/.

status.description: A paused agent keeps its work and takes none; a retired one is kept only so that its past events still name someone.

preauthorized_external_tools.description: External-effect tools this agent may use without asking the human each time (spec 5.6).

grants.description: Permission tiers this agent holds on top of its role's defaults (spec 5.6).

revokes.description: Permission tiers this agent does not hold, whatever its role's defaults say (spec 5.6: a role's tiers are the user's to override, which means taking one away as well as adding one). Taking away wins over granting.

mcp_servers.description: The connectors this agent's task sessions get (spec 5.6). Any agent may have one; team.propose gives the ui_ux_designer playwright.

model.description: The agent's own model and effort. Either may be left out, and the role's stands in for it: changing how carefully an agent works never changes what it runs on.

id.description: The provider's model id, exactly as the runtime reports it in usage, so that the price table can be asked about it.

effort.description: How hard the model thinks. The runtime passes this value to the program as it is (farik_runtime::SessionSpec::effort).

daily_usd.description: What the team may spend in a day before it pauses (spec 5.5). Left out, the day has no dollar limit: Farik ships none (ADR 0015). A sprint's own budget belongs to the sprint, not here.

sessionLimits.description: Overrides for one session's limits. What is left out keeps the role's default (farik-core's default_session_limits). The ceiling is the largest integer JSON holds exactly: a number past it is refused here, naming the field, rather than by the typed build, naming serde.

human_accepts_contracts.description: Which contracts wait for the human's acceptance (spec 5.16). `high_risk` is the default the first run writes.

wip_limit_per_agent.description: How many tasks one agent may hold that are neither accepted nor cancelled (spec 5.2). Zero refuses every assignment, which is how a team pauses an agent without retiring it.

blocked_limit_hours.description: How long a task may stay blocked before it escalates (spec 5.7).

max_iterations.description: How many times a task may be rejected before it escalates (spec 5.7).

integration.description: What happens to a task's branch after it is accepted (spec 5.14).

integration_branch.description: The branch accepted work integrates into. Left out, it is the repository's default branch (spec 5.14).

ambient_messages_per_sprint.description: How many unprompted messages each agent may post in the channel per sprint, or per UTC day while no sprint is open (spec 5.9). Left out, one.

escalation_age_hours.description: How long an open escalation may wait on the human before the aged rule ages it and says so in the channel (spec 5.7). Left out, a day.

memory_cap_tokens.description: How long each agent's notebook, .farik/agents/<id>/memory.md, may be, in tokens counted as a quarter of its characters; a longer write is refused (spec 5.8). Left out, 8000.

plan_in_sprints.description: Whether the team plans its work in sprints (ADR 0028): ready tasks wait in the Backlog until a sprint plans them, and no task is assigned outside the open sprint. Left out, false, so a team file written before the key works as it did; setup and farik init write true.

required.description: Whether every contract's plan is checked before work starts (spec 5.3). Left out, always.

default: Does the task fit its budget?
Would its checks notice if the work went wrong the way its intent worries about?
questions.description: What the judge answers about each plan, one answer per question. Left out, the two of spec 5.3. validate_team refuses none while required is always.

judge.description: Who checks plans. `auto` is the first active agent of the Architect, the Scrum Master and the Product Manager, in that order (the founder, 2026-09-29). A named judge must be an active agent (validate_team).

judgment.description: The plan check (spec 5.3). Left out, every plan is checked by the defaults.

run_commands.description: Whether Developers and Architects run commands (the execute tier). Farik still runs every check itself. Left out, true.

push.description: Whether Developers push and open pull requests (the git_remote tier). Left out, false.

permissions.description: The team's answers to what its agents may do, applied to every agent of the role before the agent's own grants and revokes (spec 5.6).

protected_paths.description: Globs no tool may read or write, whatever its tier (spec 5.6). Left out, the five farik-core ships.

allowed_paths_ceiling.description: Globs a contract's allowed_paths must fall within. Empty means no ceiling.

required_criteria.description: Verification methods every contract must have at least one criterion of.

require_new_tests.description: Whether every `test` criterion must set new_tests_required.

max_task_budget_usd.description: The most one task's budget may be. Left out, no cap: Farik ships no dollar limit (ADR 0015). An absent rule narrows nothing, and so it loosens nothing either (spec 5.12).

forbidden_commands.description: ECMAScript regular expressions a command must not match (spec 5.12).

document_paths.description: Globs every allowed path of a task not assigned to the software_developer or the ui_ux_designer must fall within: only the Developer and the UI/UX Designer change code (spec 5.12). Left out, docs/**, **/*.md and CHANGELOG.md; an empty list means no task but a Developer's or a Designer's can be ready.

ui_paths.description: Globs a software_developer's task diff is matched against when it enters verifying: a match makes it a UI change, which the ui_ux_designer design-reviews before the reviewer (ADR 0026, spec 5.12). Left out, the seven design globs; an empty list leaves only the contract's ui_change to say so.
